 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Brendon McCullum believes turning Harry Brook and Tom Banton into credible off-spinners can help England challenge for next year's World Cup.
 The wicket that sealed England's 2-1 series victory against Australia in Hobart on Wednesday was taken by captain Brook, as he bowled for the first time in his ODI career. Banton, who often keeps wicket, also bowled a game earlier in Adelaide as England neared victory.
 Opening batsman Banton had also bowled in England's warm-up match at the Waca this month, taking the wicket of former Australia all-rounder Ashton Agar.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rather than novelty japes, white-ball coach McCullum said turning the pair into genuine bowling options is part of England's plan as they build towards a gruelling World Cup next year in which his team is scheduled to play across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. A small squad of only 15 demands adaptable cricketers. McCullum sees New Zealanders Michael Bracewell and Glenn Phillips as inspiration for the pair and England believe Banton's high-release point can make him a threat.
 "In terms of Banton and Brook's bowling, Michael Bracewell and Glenn Phillips started off as wicketkeepers, then bowled a few overs in the nets, and the next thing you know they are doing it in a game," he said. "Now they are both Test spinners.
 "These guys are talented, there is something there. We are looking at a World Cup in 12 months' time, and no one knows what the conditions are going to be like. You could end up on a pitch that is exploding and need some options. We will keep encouraging them to do that. That World Cup is potentially 13 games in three different countries, fresh pitches, there's not much data on how those pitches will play, no one really knows. These are skilled players who can pivot in game and contribute on a surface.
 "It's like your bowlers – you encourage them to practise batting, because we have seen the likes of Gus Atkinson, how valuable his runs have been for us."
 Tom Banton took the wicket of former Australia all-rounder Ashton Agar in England's warm-up match at the Waca earlier this month - Getty Images/Paul Kane
 Brook has bowled very occasionally in Test cricket, even picking up the wicket of the great Kane Williamson in Wellington in 2023, strangled down the leg side. But that was with wrong-footed medium pacers, whereas McCullum now has both men practising off-spin. It is part of a wider tactical experimentation that saw Jofra Archer promoted to No 6 in the batting order as a chaos-causing pinch-hitter in Hobart. Archer made seven, but McCullum reflected: "We made a play and it didn't work out, but no one ever regretted making a positive play."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement England also have a part-time off-spinner in Will Jacks, but are without Jacob Bethell , who undergoes knee surgery on Thursday and does not have a timeframe for his return.
 The move also comes at a time when their greatest white-ball spinner, Adil Rashid, appears to be drifting out of the ODI side. Liam Dawson, who was superb in the victory in Hobart, has been preferred for his left-arm orthodox, and McCullum could not guarantee Rashid a spot in England's first-choice T20 side either. The first of five T20s is at the MCG on Saturday, with England significantly depleted following the departures of key multi-format players, who are preparing for the Tests in South Africa this Christmas.
 "It is always conditions dependent," said McCullum. "We have to look at conditions and opposition and pick the team that gives the best chance of winning. Rash is a great bowler, so is Daws. Daws has done brilliantly since coming in, but that is no slight on Rash. Daws has really put his hand up and performed.
 "All players are disappointed when they miss out but Rash is a team player who has been around for a long time. He loves getting the best out of people, and he always invests."
